title: ‘It’s Triage’: California’s Next Governor Will Face Destabilizing Surge in Uninsured
summary: The nation’s uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California’s next governor as states stare down the biggest rise in the uninsured rate in a generation.

title: The Market Forces Quietly Adding Thousands to Patient Bills
summary: The true cost of “vertical integration”: patients directed to a higher-priced location for procedures. Or forced to buy from their insurer’s wholly owned pharmacy, which may not stock the drug prescribed or provide it at the lowest price.

title: With Midterms Looming, Journalists Consider Measles, Food Recalls, and Obamacare
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Trump and Kennedy’s Health Industry Deals Haven’t Been Enforced and Are at Risk of Vanishing
summary: The agreements, covering issues like drug pricing, reducing the use of synthetic food dyes, and cutting back on insurance prior authorization rules, were announced with fanfare and touted as victories. But it’s not clear whether they’ll result in lasting change.

title: High Fertility Costs Push Americans Abroad for IVF Treatment
summary: Despite President Donald Trump’s promises to make fertility treatment more affordable, the overall costs for one IVF cycle in the U.S. remain in the tens of thousands of dollars. So more Americans than ever are going to Europe to seek IVF treatment for a fraction of the cost.

title: Why Older Pedestrians Fare Worse in Car Crashes
summary: People age 65 and up are more likely than other age groups to die after being hit by a vehicle.

title: A State Gave Sheriffs 20% of Its Opioid Settlement Cash. We Followed the Money.
summary: Opioid settlement cash was meant to abate the addiction crisis. But a new investigation reveals millions in Louisiana was spent on law enforcement gear and police technology instead of lifesaving treatment.

title: A Camp for Children With Brain Injuries Zips Ahead, Despite Federal Uncertainty
summary: Federal programs that support brain injury research and services are in flux, with lapsed legislation and a diminished injury-tracking workforce. Still, in rural Pennsylvania, children with acquired brain injuries gathered for a summer camp that emphasized community, confidence, and fun.

title: $50B Rural Health Transformation Program Needs More Transparency, Groups Say
summary: States must submit Rural Health Transformation Program progress reports to the federal government, but they aren’t required to proactively post those reports, or related information, publicly.
